root_cause.text: xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work in the XFS xattr leaf block code only adjusted a freemap entry when its base exactly matched the old end of the entry array, even though the freemap is non-comprehensive, leaving other freemap entries overlapping the expanded leaf entry array after new xattrs were added.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly shows freemap[1] starting at byte 388 while the entries array ended at 448/456 and explains that after growing the array “freemap[1] hasn't been updated, and now the entries array and the free space claim the same space”; the patch changes the logic from `if (ichdr->freemap[i].base == tmp)` to also handle any `freemap[i].size > 0 && freemap[i].base < new_end`, adjusting all overlapping freemap entries.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add old_end and new_end local variables in xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work to support forthcoming logic changes.
intent_record.what: A new local variable declaration was added in xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work(): two integers named old_end and new_end are introduced alongside the existing local variables.
intent_record.how: This change by itself only makes additional integer storage available within the function for later use and does not alter runtime behavior in the shown hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix leaf attribute freemap updates so expanding the leaf entry array correctly removes or shifts overlapping free-space regions.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a single calculation of the old leaf entry array end (`tmp`) and a matching freemap adjustment with explicit `new_end` and `old_end` calculations, updates the assertion to require `firstused >= new_end`, and changes the freemap update loop to compute a per-entry `diff` that either shifts a free region starting exactly at the old array end by one entry size or shifts any non-empty free region whose base falls before `new_end` upward by the overlap amount, while reducing its size by the minimum of its size and that `diff`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when a new leaf entry enlarges the leaf entry array, the code now correctly adjusts free space map entries not only when free space began exactly at the previous array boundary, but also when a freemap region starts inside the space newly occupied by the expanded array. This prevents the freemap from describing space that now belongs to the entry array, avoiding incorrect free-space accounting and potential overlap/corruption during later allocations.

relevance_review.reason: This change is in the exact affected function and introduces old_end/new_end variables specifically to support logic for tracking the entry array's previous and expanded bounds, which is central to fixing freemap overlap handling in the root cause.

The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes leaf attribute freemap handling when the leaf entry array expands, ensuring overlapping free-space regions are removed or shifted instead of only adjusting an entry whose base exactly matched the old array end.

candidates.rationale: This exact-match condition is the root cause: it updates a freemap entry only when its base equals the old end of the entry array, missing freemap entries that overlap the expanded array but start earlier or later.
This adjustment is only valid for the exact-match case and reflects the flawed assumption that only one freemap entry beginning at tmp must be shifted when the entry array grows.
This size reduction is paired with the exact-base check and therefore only shrinks one matching freemap region, leaving other overlapping free regions stale and inconsistent.
Using only the old end position tmp as the sole comparison point contributes to the bug because overlap must be determined across a range, not only by equality with the old array end.

vuln_statements.explanation: This exact-match check is the root cause of the vulnerability. It only updates a freemap entry whose base exactly equals the old end of the leaf entry array, but the freemap is non-comprehensive and may contain entries that overlap the expanded array without starting exactly at tmp. Those overlapping entries are left stale, causing inconsistent free-space tracking after adding new xattrs.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains the exact freemap-adjustment logic after expanding the leaf entry array. The vulnerable construct is present at lines 1422-1426: `for (i = 0; i < XFS_ATTR_LEAF_MAPSIZE; i++) { if (ichdr->freemap[i].base == tmp) { ichdr->freemap[i].base += sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t); ichdr->freemap[i].size -= sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t); } }`. Per the root cause, this code only updates a freemap entry when `freemap[i].base` exactly equals `tmp` (the old end of the entry array, computed at lines 1419-1420). Because the freemap is non-comprehensive, other freemap entries can overlap the newly expanded entry array even if their base is not exactly `tmp`, and this code does not adjust them. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present. The fix is not present because there is no broader overlap check or correction for freemap extents that intersect the expanded entry array; only exact-base matches are handled.
